subject: physics
title: Mechanics Adventure 1: Kinematics and SUVAT
welcome_lead: Today you'll launch a projectile using SUVAT equations.
meta_desc: IBDP Physics — kinematics, SUVAT equations, displacement-time and velocity-time graphs, projectiles.
final_note: You learned SUVAT links s, u, v, a, t under constant acceleration; v-t graphs show velocity (slope = a, area = s); projectiles split into independent x/y motion.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Five equations link 5 variables:

- v = u + at
- s = ut + ½at²
- s = ½(u+v)t
- v² = u² + 2as
- s = vt − ½at²

Choose the one with 4 known + 1 unknown. g = 9.81 m/s² downward near Earth.

On a velocity-time graph:
- Slope = acceleration.
- Area = displacement.

Constant velocity: horizontal line.
Uniform acceleration: straight diagonal.
Deceleration: negative slope.

x and y are independent. Horizontal: u_x = constant.
Vertical: u_y, a_y = -g.

Time of flight (level surface): t = 2u sinθ / g.
Range: R = u² sin(2θ) / g (maximum at θ = 45°).
Max height: H = u² sin²θ / (2g).

Example: ball thrown at 20 m/s at 30°. Time = 2(20)(0.5)/9.81 = 2.04 s. Range = 35.3 m.
